title: Vibecheck assessment envelope v1
description: Canonical envelope for a context-aware, risk-based Vibecheck assessment. Normative design: rfcs/0001-assessment-schema-v1.md. Syntactic validation is supplemented by semantic rules in scripts/canonical.py, scripts/actions.py and scripts/authz.py. Readers MUST ignore unknown fields and MUST preserve them when rewriting. Schema version 1.1.0 added context/risk/readiness, 1.2.0 added founder scenarios and completeness-safe reports, 1.3.0 added the versioned Action/Procedure registry, exact-attempt consent and evidence-backed completion, and 1.4.0 adds authorization-coverage cells, the representative-object inventory and staged remediation checkpoints.

control_registry.description: Which control registry version control_ids resolve against.

action_registry.description: Version of the Action/Procedure/ProcedureAttempt contract used by this envelope. Required semantically for schema 1.3+ envelopes that contain any of those records.

coverage_model.description: Version of the authorization-coverage model that evidence coverage cells and the representative-object inventory resolve against (schema/authz-coverage.v1.json).

provider_registry.description: Version of the verification-provider registry the capability records in `providers` were taken from, and the selection policy that chose between them (schema/provider-registry.v1.json).

control_id.description: Stable semantic control ID: vibecheck.control.<namespace>.<slug>. Never reused, never renamed; deprecation only via superseded_by in the registry.

environment.description: Standard environment or a documented x_ extension (extensions must be declared in context.extensions).

intended_use.description: Standard intended use or a documented x_ extension.

scope_pair.description: Readiness and contextual risk are always scoped to an explicit environment + intended-use pair.

context_field.description: One captured context fact together with how it came to be known. The state is never optional: a recorded value whose provenance is missing cannot be told apart from a guess. unknown and conflicting are treated identically by the risk derivation, and neither may be resolved silently toward the benign value.

value.description: A value id from the matching dimension in schema/vibecheck.context.v1.json.

source.description: Who confirmed it, or what artifact it was inferred from.

candidates.description: The disagreeing values, when the state is conflicting.

allOf.$comment: An unknown field may not carry a value: that is how unknown silently becomes the benign answer.

compensating_control.description: A measure already in place that lowers how likely a weakness is to be exercised in this context. It may reduce the exposure input by at most one step and never the impact (rule R7), and only while at least one cited evidence record is current (rule R15). enforced_by names the mechanism or accountable person: an intention is not a compensating control.

applies_to.description: Which risks this measure may reduce. An empty or absent applies_to means it applies to none: scope is stated, never assumed.

readiness_condition.description: When true, the measure also becomes an enforceable condition on any conditional readiness that leans on it.

derivation_record.description: How a derived object was computed, so the same normalized inputs can be shown to produce the same output. Present on machine-derived risks, readiness, scenarios and reports; absent on hand-authored ones.

unknown_inputs.description: Context dimensions that were unknown or conflicting and therefore forced an unknown input.

application_context.description: Versioned application context. Assessment conclusions are only as good as this context; its confirmation state is part of the record. The context has its own revision, confirmation date, expiry and reassessment triggers, all independent of the source-code fingerprint: changing what the application is for does not pretend the code changed, and changing the code does not pretend the context was reconfirmed.

context_model.description: Which dimension model the profile keys and values resolve against.

context_fingerprint.description: Digest of the context content itself. Distinct from confirmation.source_fingerprint, which digests the reviewed source tree.

profile.description: The captured context dimensions, keyed by dimension id from the context model (lifecycle, audience_scale, network_exposure, authentication, tenancy, data_sensitivity, financial_operations, privileged_operations, business_criticality).

authorization_objects.description: The representative private object types this application holds, one entry per class the review treats as representative. This inventory is what makes authorization coverage measurable: required cells are generated from it, and with no inventory coverage is unestablished rather than met. Excluding an object as intended_public takes a confirmed decision.

object_class.description: A class from the coverage model: user_owned_record, tenant_scoped_record, admin_or_privileged_record, credential_or_token_record, file_or_storage_object, reference_data, unclassified.

locator.description: Where the object lives, e.g. public.orders or storage:invoices. For a PostgREST table in its default schema, a bare probe name such as orders resolves to the qualified inventory locator public.orders; other schema prefixes remain distinct.

intent.description: Whether the owner means this object to be reachable without authorization. unknown is not intended_public.

current_scope.description: Where the application actually is today. Risks for this scope carry the current horizon; every other target scope is event-triggered.

target_scopes.description: The environment + intended-use pairs this assessment covers. The first entry is the primary confirmed target.

extensions.description: Documented x_ extension values. Each must state which standard value its readiness semantics inherit from (conservatively: the more exposed one).

signal.description: Raw tool output. A signal asserts nothing on its own: it has no status, verdict, or direction.

evidence.description: A scoped observation about one or more controls. Evidence can support, refute, or be neutral toward the claim that the control requirement is met. It can NEVER carry a control status: the fields status/verdict/control_status/assessment_status are structurally forbidden.

operation.description: What was actually done, e.g. static_pattern_scan, http_select_anon_head.

scope.description: What the observation covers and its limits, e.g. 'sampled last 50 commits only'.

claim.description: The claim the direction refers to. The claim statement is always phrased as 'the control requirement is met'; refuting evidence indicates violation.

aspect.description: Which facet of the control this evidence touches, when partial.

direction.description: Relative to claim.statement. NO_SIGNAL-class results are neutral: absence of a signal is not evidence of absence.

strength.description: decisive: the observation settles its claim within its stated scope. indicative: material for a human decision (all regex/path heuristics are at most indicative).

authorization.description: Required when producing the evidence needed authorization (live probes, account access).

coverage.description: Authorization cells this observation actually covers. One cell is one (object, actor, operation) in one environment; it is never generalized to another object, operation, actor or environment, and never to the control as a whole (rule R20). Static source analysis never fills a cell.

object_ref.description: The exact object observed, e.g. public.orders.

object_id.description: The inventory entry this object is, when it is a declared representative object.

object_class.description: Class from the coverage model; unclassified when nobody has classified this object yet.

observed.description: What the request did, not what it means. inconclusive covers invalid keys, expired tokens, network failures, empty tables and non-200 responses that may not be policy; it never counts as denied.

instance.description: The exact record, row or object the observation used.

assessment.description: A human or accountable-process decision about one control, based on referenced evidence. Immutable; corrections happen via a superseding assessment. Intrinsic severity lives in the control registry, never here; contextual risk lives in a separate risk object.

status.description: answered / needs_specialist are only valid for screening controls (rule R5). risk_accepted is never valid for Critical-severity controls (rule R5).

conflicts.description: Evidence that disagrees with the chosen status. Disagreement is recorded, never silently overwritten; a pass with an unresolved conflict is invalid (rule R4).

contextual_risk.description: Contextual risk for one or more controls (or a scenario) in one environment + intended-use scope. level MUST equal the shipped matrix lookup of inputs.impact x inputs.exposure unless a downgrade object is present (rule R6). Any unknown input makes level unknown. Unknown is never rendered or treated as low.

affected.description: Assets/outcomes at stake in this scope.

actor.description: Threat or failure actor, where meaningful for the domain.

plausibility_rationale.description: Why this exposure level: exploitability for security, failure plausibility for reliability, applicability/materiality for compliance, manifestation likelihood for product.

compensating_control_id.description: The context measure this came from, so the risk's freshness can be traced back to the measure's own expiry.

downgrade.description: Explicit override BELOW the matrix result. At most one level down, with rationale and current supporting evidence (rule R6). Overrides above the matrix result need no ceremony.

conflicts.description: How conflicting inputs were treated; unresolved conflicts force level unknown (rule R6).

risk_scenario.description: Founder-facing failure narrative grounded in one or more contextual risks. A scenario is a way of reading assessments, never a re-assessment of them: it may not carry a control status, an intrinsic severity or an acceptance record (rules R12, R14), and the levels it reports come from the risks it references.

title.description: Default-language (en) title; wording carries every supported language.

narrative.description: Default-language (en) narrative; wording carries every supported language.

group_id.description: Which failure story this scenario tells, per schema/report-derivation.v1.json.

procedure_refs.description: Procedures reachable through the linked actions, retained for direct appendix traceability.

wording.description: Per-language title and narrative. Translation is presentation: it never changes which controls, risks or evidence the scenario references.

risk_by_scope.description: The scenario's level per environment + intended use and horizon, so 'fine today, critical at launch' stays two readings instead of one average.

action.description: A required outcome. Founder labels ('Fix now', 'Before public launch', ...) are DERIVED display text from urgency + deadline + blocking_scope, never stored as the scheduling model.

action_key.description: Stable lineage identity shared by all revisions of this Action.

priority.description: Ordering importance, separate from when work starts (urgency) and what transition it blocks (deadline/blocking_scope).

reassess_trigger.description: When this deadline policy itself must be revisited.

blocking_scope.description: Environment + intended-use pairs that must not proceed until this action is done. Empty array means non-blocking.

decision_ref.description: Required semantically for a rejected Action unless the decision is captured in note.

success_evidence.description: What evidence closes this action. A disappeared warning is never sufficient.

required_stages.description: Remediation checkpoints this Action must pass before it can be done, in policy order. Each one needs its own authorized, succeeded attempt with produced evidence; a missing deployment leaves the Action incomplete however good the patch looks (rule R21).

procedure.description: One executable method for achieving an Action. Fields are orthogonal: what role runs it, through what mechanism, with what effects, under what authorization.

procedure_key.description: Stable lineage identity shared by immutable revisions of this Procedure.

execution_mode.description: How the method is carried out. This is independent of executor_role and never implies authorization.

stage.description: Which remediation checkpoint this method performs. Patching the repository, deploying it, and verifying the deployed behaviour are authorized and evidenced separately (rule R21, schema/action-policy.v1.json).

allOf.$comment: Rule R11 (schema-enforceable half): any write/destructive/deployment/data/external-account effect requires explicit consent.

procedure_attempt.description: One authorized execution of a procedure: exact authorization, what happened, what evidence it produced, and which reassessments followed.

authorization_id.description: Single-use authorization record identity; unique across attempts.

attempt_ref.description: Binds this embedded authorization to one exact attempt.

scope.description: Exactly what was authorized, no more.

record.description: Consent provenance: where the authorization record lives.

execution_context.description: Concrete place and revision where this attempt ran, distinct from the assessment environment label.

source_ref.description: Branch, commit, deployment or configuration revision.

input_refs.description: References only. Secret or sensitive input values never enter an attempt record.

effects_observed.description: Legacy free-text observation; schema 1.3 uses side_effects_observed.

change_control.description: Diff-first and branch-first record for a repository_patch attempt: the exact diff that was shown before authorization, the branch it was written to, and who approved it when. An approval later than started_at is not diff-first (rule R21).

review_record.description: Where the approval lives: pull request, chat transcript, ticket.

provider_capability.description: What a verification provider can observe, at what cost and side effect, so provider selection is explicit and safe. The bundled capabilities and the deterministic selection policy that reads them live in schema/provider-registry.v1.json; a capability recorded here is the one an envelope actually exercised.

summary_en.description: One sentence on what running this provider actually does.

executor_role.description: Who has to run it. A method nobody available can execute is unavailable, however strong it is.

mechanism.description: The exact tool, script or documented procedure.

availability.description: Whether this provider can run here at all. A provider that is not bundled and whose tools are absent is a coverage gap naming an install, never a silent skip.

required_targets.description: What has to exist for the provider to have anything to observe, e.g. supabase_project, deployed_web_app, source_tree. A missing target makes the provider inapplicable rather than withheld.

required_inputs.description: Inputs and data fixtures the run needs: credentials, base URLs, a known private record, a maintained flow spec. Missing ones exclude the provider and name themselves in the authorization request.

secret.description: True when supplying it is handing over a credential.

required_for.description: Controls this input is needed for; absent means every control the provider covers.

operations.description: How the observation is made, e.g. static_pattern_scan or http_select_anon_head. Not to be confused with cells.operations, which is what the observed actor tried to do.

subjects.description: Subject kinds this provider can observe for the control.

max_strength.description: Best evidence strength this provider can produce for this control. Providers never produce control-wide conclusions.

fills_coverage_cell.description: Whether an observation here fills an authorization coverage cell. Only a live observation of the deployment may: source analysis is structurally refused a cell (rule R20), so a source-reading provider that set this true would be claiming something it cannot see.

cells.description: Which (actor, operation, object class) cells this provider can observe. This is what makes coverage requirements operation- and subject-specific rather than 'checks authorization'.

requires_effects.description: Effects that covering these cells would exercise beyond the provider's default posture, e.g. write for an insert probe. Ungranted, they exclude these cells while leaving the provider's read coverage available.

closure_threshold.description: What result, in what scope, would let an assessor close the aspect this provider covers.

from_rule.description: Set when this entry was expanded from a registry coverage rule rather than written out.

environments_note.description: Why this provider's observations count for those environments, where that is not obvious.

human_effort.description: What it costs a person, which is the cost that decides whether a manual method is repeated after the next deploy.

network.description: Whether running the provider reaches anything outside this machine. Kept separate from data_egress: a request that leaves the machine is one question, and what it carries out with it is another.

opt_in_flags.description: Flags that turn on network access that is off by default, e.g. --online-audit.

deployment.description: Whether running the provider changes what is running in an environment. A verification provider that deploys is not verifying anything (rule R21).

opt_in_flags.description: Flags that unlock write/destructive behavior, e.g. --write-probe.

run_semantics.description: How a run of this provider ends when it does not end cleanly. An external tool is not under vibecheck's control, so what a timeout, a cancellation, a crash and a partial result mean for the coverage it claimed has to be stated rather than assumed: a scan that stopped early covers what it reached and nothing else, and that is never the same as a clean result.

typical_validity.description: ISO-8601 duration or prose, e.g. 'P30D' or 'until next deploy'.

readiness.description: Readiness for exactly one environment + intended-use pair. States must never be rendered as 'secure' or as certification. Precedence when deriving: blocked > incomplete > conditional > no_known_blocker.

ref.description: asm-/rsk-/act- id of the blocking record.

unknown_id.description: Stable id for this unknown, so the report can state it exactly once and prove it did (rule R12). Derived from the scope and what the unknown is about; several unknowns have no single object behind them and would otherwise be unaddressable.

material.description: true when this unknown could hide a blocker; any material unknown keeps state at incomplete or worse.

enforced_by.description: The mechanism or person enforcing the condition, not an aspiration.

blocked_transitions.description: More exposed scopes this readiness does not cover, with their own state and why moving there is not possible on today's evidence. Keeps a narrow conditional or no-known-blocker state from reading as permission to widen the scope.

framework_verdict.description: The legacy checklist verdict computed from the same assessments, kept beside the scoped readiness state instead of being replaced by it. explanation is always required, so a difference between the two is explained rather than hidden.

report.description: Presentation contract. The 3-5 headline cap is a summary rule only: every mandatory disclosure set must be complete regardless (rule R12). audience and language name the default rendering; the sets, the ranking and the control identities they reference are the same in every profile and language.

scenario_ranking.description: Every scenario in reading order with the inputs that put it there, headline or not. A scenario below the cap keeps its rank, its refs and its appendix entry.

specialist_assessment_refs.description: Compatibility fallback for needs_specialist assessments not yet materialized as Increment-4 Actions.

disclosure_placement.description: Where each mandatory ref is rendered: exactly one visible slot per ref, either the headline scenario that tells its story or the mandatory section. Stored so that 'it was shown' is checkable rather than claimed.

category.description: Primary category under which this ref is visibly listed when it is not covered by a headline.

categories.description: Every mandatory set this ref belongs to. A single action can be an incident, a specialist escalation and a deadline blocker while retaining exactly one visible placement.

context_summary.description: The confirmed intended-use context the whole report is scoped to, with its revision and freshness.

appendix.description: The reviewer record kept behind the founder summary: the full framework view plus every assessment, evidence item, risk, scenario and action, whether or not it reached the headlines.

legacy_action_view.description: Lossy derived AUTO/PROPOSE/ADVISORY compatibility view. Never authorization.

framework_mapping.description: Lossless mapping between canonical control IDs and an external framework view. vibecheck_v1 is the existing 89-item checklist: item numbers, categories, EN/ET wording, verification metadata, scanner checks, and workbook profiles all round-trip.

status_map.description: Canonical status -> framework display wording per language.

provenance.description: How this framework mapping was established and how it is maintained. Historical envelopes keep the mapping version that was current at assessment time; a mapping change ships as a new version, never an in-place rewrite of past assessments.

related_control_ids.description: Optional other controls this framework item also maps to. Framework items and controls are many-to-many: a framework item may span several controls, and a control may satisfy several items across frameworks. The primary control_id keeps the entry addressable; related ids record the reuse edges without duplicating control records.

kind.description: Triage rows are screening: statuses answered/needs_specialist apply.

provenance.description: Optional per-entry provenance: why this framework item maps to this control. Framework items and controls are many-to-many; provenance records the rationale and review for a specific mapping edge.
